summary: Backend-only iteration 5 verifying PROMPT 03 authorization hardening (RBAC + strict tenant isolation + API-key scoping + feature entitlement enforcement + resource ownership). Ran full pytest suite serially (-n0) as instructed: 60/60 passed in 33.7s. This includes all 10 new authz/isolation tests in tests/test_authz_isolation.py plus the pre-existing 50 tests (foundation, extended, commerce, iteration3, auth_security). Coverage confirmed for every item in the review request: (1) RBAC server-side — a ClientOps user (only payment.create+refund.create) gets 403 on POST /api/providers and POST /api/users; (2) tenant isolation on GET with ?tenant_id=<other> returns 403 for /api/payments, /api/settlements, /api/ledger/entries, /api/api-keys, /api/webhooks/deliveries, /api/reports/scheduled, and the CSV export /api/reports/export/payments.csv; (3) tenant isolation on POST returns 403 and guessed IDs for GET /api/payments/{id} and POST /api/payments/{id}/refunds of another tenant's payment return 404; (4) API keys are tenant-scoped — a checkout session created with tenant A's key is not visible in tenant B's list, a revoked key returns 401 on /api/v1/checkout/sessions, a bogus key returns 401 without leaking info, and creation returns the secret exactly once (list responses expose only last4); (5) feature entitlement enforced on backend — disabling 'refunds' on a tenant causes POST /api/payments/{id}/refunds to return 403; re-enabling returns 200; (6) Super Admin platform access across tenants still works (GET /api/payments?tenant_id=<any> = 200); (7) legitimate same-tenant client access works (GET+POST /api/payments = 200); (8) regression: MFA/session/password-reset (test_auth_security) and all business modules (payments, refunds, ledger, settlements, checkout, webhooks, reports, api keys, tenants, access control, feature flags, audit, monitoring) still pass. Additional ad-hoc curls: super-admin cross-tenant GET returned 200; bogus X-API-Key returned 401. No critical or minor bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: feature_enabled/require_feature semantics (missing flag => allowed, disabled flag => 403) match the spec and are exercised by test_feature_entitlement_enforced_on_backend; the flag was toggled on the 'iso' tenant so it does not leak into other suites (test_extended's own toggle is now self-restoring).

Cross-tenant ID probing on payments correctly returns 404 (not 403) to avoid leaking resource existence — good IDOR-safe pattern; contrast with query-param ?tenant_id=B which returns 403 because the tenant context itself is what's being denied.

API-key secrets are returned only at creation; subsequent listing exposes last4 only, and revoked keys are rejected at /api/v1/*. Verified in test_api_key_is_tenant_scoped + test_revoked_api_key_denied.

PRE-EXISTING (unchanged from prior iteration): pytest.ini defaults to xdist parallel while webhook-lifecycle tests race on the shared 'acme' tenant → FK error under -n auto; workaround is -n0. Consider scoping webhook tests to a session-unique tenant fixture.

Minor: /api/features PATCH accepts partial updates; consider adding an audit trail entry when a feature entitlement is toggled (esp. security-sensitive ones like refunds) so tenant-admin actions are traceable.
test_credentials: admin@cloudpay.io / [REDACTED] (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md); ClientOps test users and an 'iso*' isolated tenant created at runtime by the suite.
seed_data_creation: Fresh isolated tenant per module (slug iso<rand>), a ClientOps role with only payment.create+refund.create, and one iso_<rand>@test.com user. Also created ephemeral payments, api-keys, and a refunds feature flag; state is confined to the throw-away tenant, so it does not affect acme or other suites.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Always run backend as: `cd /app/backend && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && python -m pytest tests/ -q -n0` — parallel xdist has a pre-existing race in webhook tests. Test file for this prompt: /app/backend/tests/test_authz_isolation.py (10 tests, module-scoped fixtures for admin/two_tenants/tenant_user). Feature-flag toggle side-effects are contained to the module's isolated tenant; test_extended already self-restores acme's 'refunds' flag. Auth pattern for API tests: login with JSON, then use Authorization: Bearer <access_token> from Set-Cookie (cookies are dropped over http://localhost).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs detected. Authorization sequence (authenticated user → role → permission → tenant → feature entitlement → resource ownership → allowed action) is enforced end-to-end at the API layer.
